e.etymology: From Sanskrit sahasra, thousand, a number that stands for abundance, as in the sahasranama, the thousand names of a deity. It is especially popular in Telugu families.
A blend of Taylor or Tay with Lynn, in the pattern of Kaylynn and Jaylynn.
A respelling of Eden, the garden of Genesis, from Hebrew eden, delight or pleasure.

assoc.t: the Garden of Eden in the Bible (spelled Eden)

e.etymology: From Latin Arius, Greek Areios, of Ares, the god of war. Its best-known bearer was Arius of Alexandria, an early Christian priest.
e.note: Arius was the 4th-century priest whose doctrine, Arianism, the Council of Nicaea condemned as heresy.

e.etymology: The Ukrainian form, also used in Russian alongside Artyom, of the Greek name Artemios, belonging to Artemis, the goddess of the hunt and the moon.
A respelling of Adeline, the French pet form of Adele, from the Germanic word adal, noble. Spellings with -lyn and -lyne multiplied in the US in the 2010s.
An Arabic girls' name that became popular in the 2000s. It is usually explained as moon glow, while Arabic dictionaries link it to mayyar, one who brings provisions.
A respelling of Everett that brings out the name Rhett. Everett is an English surname from the Germanic name Everard, eber, wild boar, and hard, brave.
A spelling of Ellie, the pet form of Eleanor, Ellen, Elizabeth and other El- names. Elli is the usual form in Finland, Germany and Greece.
A modern elaboration of Sol and Soleil, the Spanish and French words for sun, with the -eia ending of Leia.
A short form of Abraham, from Hebrew Avraham, which Genesis explains as father of a multitude. Honest Abe was Abraham Lincoln's nickname.
namesakes: Abraham Lincoln (16th US president, known as Honest Abe)
Abe Vigoda (actor in The Godfather and Barney Miller)

assoc.t: Abraham Lincoln, known as Honest Abe

e.etymology: A K spelling of Claire, the French form of Clara, from Latin clarus, clear, bright or famous. Saint Clare of Assisi spread the name in the Middle Ages.
A modern American blend of the Ja- prefix with the ending of Mariah and Zariah.
A modern American name pairing the Ad- of Addison and Adeline with the popular -leigh ending; also spelled Adley and Adlee.
A Spanish-language spelling in the family of Jasiel and Jaziel, names drawn from the biblical Jaasiel and Jahziel. It is used mostly by Mexican American families.
A respelling of Analía, a Spanish blend of Ana and Lía, with the -iah ending of Aaliyah and Mariah.
Known from Costa Rican goalkeeper Keylor Navas, whose fame at the 2014 World Cup and with Real Madrid spread the name among Spanish-speaking families. Its earlier origin is unclear.
namesakes: Keylor Navas (Costa Rican goalkeeper for Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain)

assoc.t: Keylor Navas, Costa Rican soccer goalkeeper

e.etymology: A short form of Naomi, from Hebrew No'omi, my pleasantness. In the Bible Naomi is the mother-in-law of Ruth.
A recent American coinage, built on the sound of Dior with a Kai- opening.
A variant spelling of Mabel, a medieval short form of Amabel, from Latin amabilis, lovable. The Mable spelling was common in the US around 1900.
An American phonetic spelling of Antoine, the French form of Anthony. Anthony comes from the Roman family name Antonius, whose original meaning is unknown.
namesakes: Antwan Patton (rapper Big Boi of OutKast)

e.etymology: From Ancient Greek kharis, grace, charm or beauty. In Greek myth Charis is one of the Charites, the Graces, and the same word is the New Testament's term for divine grace.
e.note: Pronunciation varies (KAIR-iss, KAR-iss, sometimes CHAIR-iss), so expect to correct people.

e.etymology: A double-s spelling of Allison. Alison was a medieval French pet form of Alice, from Old High German Adalheid, of noble kind, brought to England by the Normans.
A modern American coinage: Trey, a nickname meaning three that is often given to a third-generation namesake, with the -son ending of Grayson and Bryson.
The Spanish form of Enoch, from Hebrew Hanokh, dedicated. In Genesis, Enoch is the father of Methuselah, a man who walked with God and was taken up without dying.
A Russian variant of Irina, the Slavic form of Irene, from Greek eirene, peace. Eirene was also the Greek goddess of peace.
From Turkic arslan, lion, taken into Persian as Arsalan and carried across Iran and South Asia. Aslan, the lion of Narnia, is the same word.
From Old Norse Rúna, from rún, secret lore or rune; the feminine of Rune. Also a Japanese girls' name written with various kanji, sometimes chosen as a rendering of Luna.
A modern elaboration of Ezra with the -ael ending of Israel and Azrael. Ezra is Hebrew for help.
e.note: One letter away from Azrael, the angel of death in Jewish and Islamic tradition.

e.etymology: A spelling of Brendan shaped by Brandon. Brendan is the English form of Irish Bréanainn, a saint's name that goes back to an old Celtic word for prince.
namesakes: Brendon Urie (frontman of Panic! at the Disco)

e.etymology: A spelling of Braden, an Irish surname from Ó Bradáin, descendant of Bradán, a byname from bradán, salmon. It rose in the 1990s and 2000s alongside Aiden, Caden and Jaden.
